title.zh: 卷405 列傳一百九十二 曾国籓
title.raw: 卷405 列傳一百九十二 曾国籓

sentences.zh: 列傳一百九十二

translations.literal: Biographies 192
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 192

sentences.zh: 曾國籓

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan

sentences.zh: 曾國籓，初名子城，字滌生，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan, original name Zicheng, courtesy name Disheng, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan, whose original name was Zicheng and whose courtesy name was Disheng, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 家世農。

translations.literal: His family had been farmers for generations.
translations.idiomatic: His family had farmed for generations.

sentences.zh: 祖玉屏，始慕鄉學。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yuping first took an interest in village schooling.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yuping was the first in the family to turn toward village learning.

sentences.zh: 父麟書，為縣學生，以孝聞。

translations.literal: His father Linshu was a student of the district school and was renowned for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His father Linshu held the rank of district-school student and was known throughout the region for his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 國籓，道光十八年進士。

translations.literal: Guofan passed the jinshi examination in the eighteenth year of Daoguang (1838).
translations.idiomatic: Guofan received his jinshi degree in the eighteenth year of Daoguang (1838).

sentences.zh: 二十三年，以檢討典試四川，再轉侍讀，累遷內閣學士、禮部侍郎，署兵部。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year (1843), as a reviser he conducted the provincial examination in Sichuan, was later transferred to reader-in-waiting, and was successively promoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat and Vice Minister of Rites, while also acting as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of the reign (1843), serving as a reviser he presided over the Sichuan provincial examinations, was later made reader-in-waiting, and rose in succession to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat and Vice Minister of Rites, with concurrent charge of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 時太常寺卿唐鑑講學京師，國籓與倭仁、吳廷棟、何桂珍嚴事之，治義理之學。

translations.literal: At that time Tang Jian, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, lectured in the capital; Guofan, together with Woren, Wu Tingdong, and He Guizhen, served him with strict reverence and studied the learning of moral principle.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jian, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was then lecturing in the capital, and Guofan—along with Woren, Wu Tingdong, and He Guizhen—reverently attended him and pursued the Neo-Confucian study of moral principle.

sentences.zh: 兼友梅曾亮及邵懿辰、劉傳瑩諸人，為詞章考據，尤留心天下人材。

translations.literal: He also befriended Mei Cengliang, Shao Yichen, Liu Chuanying, and others, engaging in belles-lettres and evidential scholarship, and paid especial attention to talent throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He also kept company with Mei Cengliang, Shao Yichen, Liu Chuanying, and others in literary composition and evidential scholarship, while keeping a keen eye on men of talent across the empire.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，廣西兵事起，詔群臣言得失。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xianfeng reign, military troubles broke out in Guangxi, and an edict summoned the ministers to speak on what had been gained and lost.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign, rebellion flared in Guangxi, and the throne ordered the ministers to speak frankly on the empire's strengths and failures.

sentences.zh: 奏陳今日急務，首在用人，人才有轉移之道，有培養之方，有考察之法。

translations.literal: In his memorial he set forth the urgent tasks of the day: first among them was the employment of men; talent had ways of being redirected, methods of cultivation, and means of investigation.
translations.idiomatic: In his memorial he declared that the day's most urgent task was putting the right men in place—that talent could be redirected, cultivated, and tested by proper methods.

sentences.zh: 上稱其剴切明辨。

translations.literal: The emperor praised it as incisive, earnest, and clear in judgment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the memorial as incisive, earnest, and lucid.

sentences.zh: 尋疏薦李棠階、吳廷棟、王慶雲、嚴正基、江忠源五人。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he memorialized recommending five men: Li Tangjie, Wu Tingdong, Wang Qingyun, Yan Zhengji, and Jiang Zhongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he submitted a memorial recommending Li Tangjie, Wu Tingdong, Wang Qingyun, Yan Zhengji, and Jiang Zhongyuan.

sentences.zh: 寇氛益熾，复上言：「國用不足，兵伍不精，二者為天下大患。

translations.literal: As the rebel menace grew fiercer, he again submitted a memorial: "Insufficient state revenue and unskilled troops—these two are the great calamities of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebel threat intensified, he memorialized again: "Insufficient revenue and unskilled troops—these are the empire's two gravest ills.

sentences.zh: 於歲入常額外，誠不可別求搜刮之術，增一分則民受一分之害。

translations.literal: Beyond the regular annual intake, one truly must not seek separate schemes of exaction; for every extra fraction levied, the people suffer a corresponding fraction of harm.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the regular annual revenue, we must not resort to new schemes of exaction—for every extra fraction taken, the people suffer proportionate harm.

sentences.zh: 至歲出之數，兵餉為鉅，綠營兵額六十四萬，常虛六七萬以資給軍用。

translations.literal: As for annual expenditure, military pay was the largest item; the Green Standard establishment numbered 640,000, yet 60,000 to 70,000 posts were habitually left vacant to fund military needs.
translations.idiomatic: Of annual outlays, military pay was the heaviest burden: the Green Standard rolls listed 640,000 men, yet 60,000 to 70,000 posts were routinely left vacant to help meet military costs.

sentences.zh: 自乾隆中增兵議起，歲糜帑二百餘萬。

translations.literal: Since the mid-Qianlong debate over increasing troops, more than two million taels were squandered each year.
translations.idiomatic: Since the mid-Qianlong debate over troop increases, the treasury had been wasting more than two million taels a year on the army.

sentences.zh: 其時大學士阿桂即憂其難繼，嘉、道間兩次議裁，不及十之四，仍宜汰五萬，復舊額。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Secretary Agui had already worried that it could not be sustained; in the Jiaqing and Daoguang reigns two reductions were debated, yet fewer than four-tenths were cut. It would still be right to trim 50,000 and restore the old establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Even then Grand Secretary Agui had warned that the burden could not be sustained; under Jiaqing and Daoguang two rounds of cuts were proposed, yet fewer than four-tenths were actually removed. He urged cutting another 50,000 men and restoring the old rolls.

sentences.zh: 自古開國之初，兵少而國強，其後兵愈多則力愈弱，餉愈多則國愈貧。

translations.literal: From antiquity, at the founding of every dynasty armies were few yet the state was strong; afterward the more troops there were, the weaker the power, and the more pay was spent, the poorer the state.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, at a dynasty's founding few troops have meant a strong state; afterward the more soldiers there are, the weaker the army grows, and the more pay is spent, the poorer the treasury becomes.

sentences.zh: 應請皇上註意將才，但使七十一鎮中有十餘鎮足為心腹，則緩急可恃矣。

translations.literal: He asked that Your Majesty attend to commanders of talent: if only a dozen or so of the seventy-one garrisons were reliable as inner forces, then in crisis or calm one could depend on them.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the emperor to cultivate commanders of real talent: if even a dozen of the seventy-one garrisons could serve as a dependable core, the throne would have forces it could trust in any emergency.

sentences.zh: 」又深痛內外臣工諂諛欺飾，無陳善責難之風。

translations.literal: " He also deeply lamented that officials within and without the court flattered, deceived, and covered up facts, with none of the spirit of presenting good counsel and holding others to account.
translations.idiomatic: " He also lamented that officials at court and in the provinces flattered, deceived, and concealed the truth, with none of the old spirit of frank counsel and mutual accountability.

sentences.zh: 因上敬陳聖德預防流弊一疏，切指帝躬，有人所難言者，上優詔答之。

translations.literal: He therefore submitted a memorial reverently setting forth sagely virtue and forestalling abuses, pointing directly at the emperor's own person in ways others found hard to speak; the emperor answered with an edict of special favor.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore submitted a memorial on cultivating imperial virtue and forestalling abuses, speaking with blunt directness to the emperor himself on matters others dared not raise; the throne answered with an edict of gracious approval.

sentences.zh: 歷署刑部、吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He served in succession as acting Vice Minister of Punishments and of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as acting Vice Minister of Punishments and of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二年，典試江西，中途丁母憂歸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng (1852), he conducted the Jiangxi provincial examination, but on the way was recalled home upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng (1852), while presiding over the Jiangxi provincial examinations, he was called home midway on news of his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 三年，粵寇破江寧，據為偽都，分黨北犯河南、直隸，天下騷動，而國籓已前奉旨辦團練於長沙。

translations.literal: In the third year (1853), the Cantonese rebels took Jiangning and made it their false capital, sent factions north to invade Henan and Zhili, and threw the realm into turmoil; Guofan had already earlier received orders to organize local militia at Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1853) the Taiping rebels seized Nanjing and made it their capital, while detachments marched north into Henan and Zhili and the empire was thrown into uproar. Guofan had already been ordered to organize local defense at Changsha.

sentences.zh: 初，國籓欲疏請終制，郭嵩燾曰：「公素具澄清之抱，今不乘時自效，如君父何？

translations.literal: At first Guofan wished to memorialize requesting to complete the full mourning period. Guo Songsong said: "Your Excellency has long cherished the resolve to set things right; if you do not seize this moment to serve, what of our sovereign and father?
translations.idiomatic: At first Guofan meant to petition for permission to observe the full three-year mourning. Guo Songsong said, "You have long aspired to set the realm to rights—if you do not seize this moment to serve, what becomes of your duty to sovereign and father?

sentences.zh: 且墨絰從戎，古制也。

translations.literal: Moreover, taking the field in mourning garb is an ancient institution."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, taking the field in mourning dress is an ancient precedent."

sentences.zh: 」遂不復辭。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he did not decline again.
translations.idiomatic: With that he did not decline again.

sentences.zh: 取明戚繼光遺法，募農民樸實壯健者，朝夕訓練之。

translations.literal: Following the legacy methods of the Ming general Qi Jiguang, he recruited plain, sturdy peasants and drilled them morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Adopting the methods left by the Ming general Qi Jiguang, he recruited plain, sturdy farmers and drilled them from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 將領率用諸生，統眾數不逾五百，號「湘勇」。

translations.literal: Commanders were generally drawn from degree-holders; each unit commanded no more than five hundred men. They were called the "Hunan Braves."
translations.idiomatic: He chose literati for his officers, kept each unit under five hundred men, and called the force the "Hunan Braves."

sentences.zh: 騰書遐邇，雖卑賤與鈞禮。

translations.literal: He sent letters far and wide and treated even the lowly as equals in courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote openly to men near and far and treated even the humble as equals.

sentences.zh: 山野材智之士感其誠，莫不往見，人人皆以曾公可與言事。

translations.literal: Talented men of the hills and wilds, moved by his sincerity, all came to see him; everyone felt that Lord Zeng was someone with whom one could discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Men of talent from the countryside, moved by his sincerity, came to see him one after another; all believed that Lord Zeng was someone with whom great affairs could be discussed.

sentences.zh: 四境土匪發，聞警即以湘勇往。

translations.literal: When bandits rose on all sides, at the first alarm he sent the Hunan Braves out.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits erupted throughout the region, he dispatched the Hunan Braves at the first alarm.

sentences.zh: 立三等法，不以煩府縣獄。

translations.literal: He established a three-grade law and did not trouble the prefectural and district prisons.
translations.idiomatic: He set up a three-tier system of justice and did not burden the regular courts.

sentences.zh: 旬月中，莠民猾胥，便宜捕斬二百餘人。

translations.literal: Within a fortnight, more than two hundred wicked commoners and crafty clerks were seized and summarily executed as expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Within a fortnight he had seized and summarily executed more than two hundred ruffians and corrupt clerks.

sentences.zh: 謗讟四起，自巡撫司道下皆心誹之，至以盛暑練操為虐士。

translations.literal: Slander arose on every side; from the governor down through the circuit and prefectural officials all secretly reviled him, even accusing him of tormenting the men by drilling in the height of summer.
translations.idiomatic: Slander spread on every side; from the governor down through the provincial bureaucracy men secretly resented him, even charging that drilling troops in midsummer was cruelty.

sentences.zh: 然見所奏輒得褒答受主知，未有以難也。

translations.literal: Yet whenever his memorials were seen they won praise and replies, and he gained the sovereign's trust; no one dared openly oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his memorials consistently won imperial praise, and he enjoyed the emperor's confidence—so none dared openly stand in his way.

sentences.zh: 一日標兵與湘勇閧，至闌入國籓行台。

translations.literal: One day the provincial garrison troops brawled with the Hunan Braves and even forced their way into Guofan's field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: One day the provincial garrison troops clashed with the Hunan Braves and even stormed into Guofan's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 國籓親訴諸巡撫，巡撫漫謝之，不為理，即日移營城外避標兵。

translations.literal: Guofan personally appealed to the governor, who gave a perfunctory apology but did nothing; that same day Guofan moved his camp outside the city walls to avoid the garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan appealed in person to the governor, who offered a perfunctory apology but took no action; that same day Guofan moved his camp outside the walls to avoid the garrison.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「曷以聞？

translations.literal: Someone said: "Why not report it?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked, "Why not report this to the throne?

sentences.zh: 」國籓歎曰：「大難未已，吾人敢以私憤瀆君父乎？

translations.literal: " Guofan sighed and said: "The great calamity is not yet over—how dare we trouble our sovereign and father with private resentment?
translations.idiomatic: Guofan sighed and said, "The great crisis is not yet past—how dare we trouble our sovereign and father with private grievances?

sentences.zh: 嘗與嵩燾、忠源論東南形勢多阻水，欲勦賊非治水師不可，乃奏請造戰艦於衡州。

translations.literal: He once discussed with Songsong and Zhongyuan how the southeast was largely cut by waterways and that to exterminate the rebels one must have a river fleet; he therefore memorialized requesting that warships be built at Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He had discussed with Guo Songsong and Jiang Zhongyuan how the southeast was a country of rivers and that suppressing the rebels required a navy; he memorialized to build warships at Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 匠卒無曉船制者，短橈長槳，出自精思，以人力勝風水，遂成大小二百四十艦。

translations.literal: Among craftsmen and soldiers none understood shipbuilding; short oars and long sweeps, devised through careful thought, used human strength to overcome wind and current, and in the end 240 large and small vessels were completed.
translations.idiomatic: None of the craftsmen or soldiers knew naval design; through careful thought he devised short oars and long sweeps so that human power could overcome wind and current, and in the end completed 240 vessels large and small.

sentences.zh: 募水陸萬人，水軍以褚汝航、楊載福、彭玉麟領之，陸軍以塔齊布、羅澤南領之。

translations.literal: He recruited ten thousand men for land and water forces; the river army was led by Chu Ruhang, Yang Zaifu, and Peng Yulin, and the land army by Taqibu and Luo Zinan.
translations.idiomatic: He raised ten thousand men for combined land and river operations: Chu Ruhang, Yang Zaifu, and Peng Yulin commanded the fleet, while Taqibu and Luo Zinan led the land forces.

sentences.zh: 賊自江西上竄，再陷九江、安慶。

translations.literal: The rebels fled up from Jiangxi and again took Jiujiang and Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels drove up from Jiangxi and again seized Jiujiang and Anqing.

sentences.zh: 忠源戰歿廬州，吳文鎔督師黃州亦敗死。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan died in battle at Luzhou; Wu Wenrong, commanding at Huangzhou, was also defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhongyuan fell in battle at Luzhou, and Wu Wenrong, commanding at Huangzhou, was likewise defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 漢陽失，武昌戒嚴，賊复乘勢擾湖南。

translations.literal: Hanyang was lost, Wuchang was placed on alert, and the rebels again took advantage of the momentum to harass Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Hanyang fell, Wuchang was placed on alert, and the rebels again swept into Hunan on the tide of victory.

sentences.zh: 國籓銳欲討賊，率水陸軍東下。

translations.literal: Guofan was eager to attack the rebels and led his land and river forces eastward downriver.
translations.idiomatic: Burning to strike at the rebels, Guofan led his combined army and fleet down the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 舟師初出湖，大風，損數十艘。

translations.literal: When the fleet first left the lake, a great wind damaged several dozen vessels.
translations.idiomatic: As the fleet first cleared the lake, a fierce gale wrecked several dozen ships.

sentences.zh: 陸師至岳州，前隊潰退，引還長沙。

translations.literal: The land army reached Yuezhou, but the vanguard broke and fell back, and he withdrew to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: The land force reached Yuezhou, but the vanguard collapsed and he was forced back to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 賊陷湘潭，邀擊靖港，又敗，國籓憤投水，幕下士章壽麟掖起之，得不死。

translations.literal: The rebels took Xiangtan; he intercepted them at Jinggang but was defeated again. In despair Guofan threw himself into the water; Zhang Shoulin, a member of his staff, pulled him up and he did not die.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels seized Xiangtan; he met them at Jinggang and was beaten again. In despair Guofan threw himself into the river, but Zhang Shoulin, a member of his staff, pulled him out and saved his life.

sentences.zh: 而同時塔齊布大破賊湘潭，國籓營長沙高峰寺，重整軍實，人人捓揄之。

translations.literal: Yet at the same time Taqibu inflicted a great defeat on the rebels at Xiangtan. Guofan encamped at Gaofeng Temple in Changsha, reorganized his army's equipment, and everyone mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at the same moment Taqibu won a crushing victory at Xiangtan. Guofan made camp at Gaofeng Temple in Changsha and set about reorganizing his forces, while men on every side mocked him.

sentences.zh: 或請增兵，國籓曰：「吾水陸萬人非不多，而遇賊即潰。

translations.literal: Some urged him to increase his forces. Guofan said: "My ten thousand on land and water are not few, yet at contact with the enemy they collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to raise more troops. Guofan said, "Ten thousand men on land and water are not too few, yet they break the moment they meet the enemy.

sentences.zh: 岳州之敗，水師拒戰者惟載福一營；

translations.literal: At the defeat at Yuezhou, of the river force only Zaifu's single battalion stood and fought;
translations.idiomatic: At Yuezhou only Yang Zaifu's single battalion among the fleet stood and fought;

sentences.zh: 湘潭之戰，陸師塔齊布、水師載福各兩營：以此知兵貴精不貴多。

translations.literal: at the battle of Xiangtan, on land Taqibu and on the water Zaifu each had but two battalions: from this one knows that troops value quality, not numbers.
translations.idiomatic: at Xiangtan Taqibu on land and Yang Zaifu on the water each had only two battalions—this shows that armies value quality, not numbers.

sentences.zh: 故諸葛敗祁山，且謀減兵損食，勤求己過，非虛言也。

translations.literal: Thus when Zhuge Liang was defeated at Qishan he even planned to reduce troops and cut rations and diligently sought his own faults—this was no empty saying.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Liang was defeated at Qishan he even planned to cut troops and rations and searched diligently for his own faults—that was no empty lesson.

sentences.zh: 且古人用兵，先明功罪賞罰。

translations.literal: Moreover, the ancients in employing troops first made merit, guilt, reward, and punishment clear.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the ancients made merit, guilt, reward, and punishment explicit before they fought.

sentences.zh: 今世亂，賢人君子皆潛伏，吾以義聲倡導，同履危亡。

translations.literal: In today's disorder worthy gentlemen are all in hiding; I have raised the call of righteousness and they share peril and ruin with me.
translations.idiomatic: In this age of chaos worthy men lie low; I rallied them with a call to righteousness, and they share my peril.

sentences.zh: 諸公之初從我，非以利動也，故於法亦有難施，其致敗由此。

translations.literal: When you gentlemen first followed me, it was not profit that moved you; therefore it is also hard to apply the law strictly, and defeat comes from this.
translations.idiomatic: You followed me at first not for profit, so it is hard to enforce discipline strictly—and that is why we have been defeated.

sentences.zh: 」諸將聞之皆服。

translations.literal: " When the generals heard this they were all convinced.
translations.idiomatic: When the generals heard this, they were all convinced.

sentences.zh: 陸師既克湘潭，巡撫、提督上功，而國籓請罪。

translations.literal: Once the land army had taken Xiangtan, the governor and provincial military commander reported merit, while Guofan asked to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: After the land force took Xiangtan, the governor and provincial commander reported the victory, while Guofan submitted a plea for punishment.

sentences.zh: 上詰責提督鮑起豹，免其官，以塔齊布代之。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Provincial Commander Bao Qibao, removed him from office, and replaced him with Taqibu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Provincial Commander Bao Qibao, stripped him of his post, and replaced him with Taqibu.

sentences.zh: 受印日，士民聚觀，嘆詫國籓為知人，而天子能明見萬里也。

translations.literal: On the day he received the seal, scholars and commoners gathered to watch and marveled that Guofan knew men and that the Son of Heaven could see clearly for ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Taqibu received his seal, crowds gathered and marveled that Guofan knew how to judge men and that the emperor could see clearly across the realm.

sentences.zh: 賊自岳州陷常德，旋北走，武昌再失。

translations.literal: The rebels, having taken Changde from Yuezhou, soon fled north, and Wuchang was lost again.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels took Changde from Yuezhou, then drove north, and Wuchang fell once more.

sentences.zh: 國籓引兵趨岳州，斬賊梟將曾天養，連戰，下城陵磯。

translations.literal: Guofan led his troops toward Yuezhou, beheaded the rebel commander Zeng Tianyang, fought successive battles, and took Chenglingji.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan marched on Yuezhou, beheaded the rebel commander Zeng Tianyang, fought a series of engagements, and captured Chenglingji.

sentences.zh: 會師金口，謀取武昌。

translations.literal: He joined forces at Jinkou and planned to take Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He concentrated his forces at Jinkou and planned the recapture of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 澤南沿江東岸攻花園寇屯，塔齊布伏兵洪山，載福舟師深入寇屯，士皆露立，不避鉛丸。

translations.literal: Zinan attacked the rebel stockade at Huayuan along the east bank; Taqibu lay in ambush at Hongshan; Zaifu's fleet drove deep into the rebel positions, and the men all stood exposed, not shunning lead shot.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Zinan struck the rebel camp at Huayuan along the east bank; Taqibu lay in ambush on Hongshan; Yang Zaifu's fleet drove deep into the enemy lines, and his men stood exposed in the open, heedless of musket fire.

sentences.zh: 武昌、漢陽賊望見官軍盛，宵遁，遂復二郡。

translations.literal: The rebels in Wuchang and Hanyang, seeing the government forces in strength, fled by night, and the two prefectures were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the government forces in overwhelming strength, the rebels in Wuchang and Hanyang fled by night, and both cities were recovered.

sentences.zh: 國籓以前靖港敗，自請奪官，至是奏上，詔署湖北巡撫，尋加兵部侍郎銜，解署任，命督師東下。

translations.literal: Guofan, because of his earlier defeat at Jinggang, had asked that his office be stripped; now his memorial was submitted, and an edict appointed him acting Governor of Hubei, soon added the rank of Vice Minister of War, relieved him of the acting post, and ordered him to command the army eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan had earlier asked to be stripped of rank after the defeat at Jinggang; when that memorial was now submitted, the throne appointed him acting Governor of Hubei, soon added Vice Minister of War, released him from the acting governorship, and ordered him to command the advance downriver.

sentences.zh: 當是時，水師奮厲無前，大破賊田家鎮，斃賊數万，至於九江，前鋒薄湖口。

translations.literal: At this time the river fleet fought with tireless advance, inflicted a great defeat on the rebels at Tianjiazhen, killed tens of thousands, reached Jiujiang, and the vanguard pressed close to Hukou.
translations.idiomatic: The fleet now fought with unstoppable fury, crushing the rebels at Tianjiazhen and killing tens of thousands, reaching Jiujiang with the vanguard pressing on Hukou.

sentences.zh: 攻梅家洲賊壘不下，駛入鄱湖。

translations.literal: They could not take the rebel fort at Meijiazhou and sailed into Poyang Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to reduce the rebel fort at Meijiazhou, they sailed into Poyang Lake.

sentences.zh: 賊築壘湖口斷其後，舟不得出，於是外江、內湖阻絕。

translations.literal: The rebels built fortifications at Hukou to cut off their rear, and the vessels could not get out; thus the outer river and inner lake were severed from each other.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fortified Hukou and cut off their retreat, trapping the ships so that the outer Yangtze and inner lake were completely cut off from each other.

sentences.zh: 外江戰船無小艇，賊乘舴艋夜襲營，擲火燒坐船，​​國籓跳而免，水師遂大亂。

translations.literal: The warships on the outer river had no small boats; the rebels used skiffs to raid the camp by night, threw fire to burn the command vessels, and Guofan leaped clear and escaped; the river army then fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The warships on the outer river had no small craft; the rebels came by night in skiffs, set fire to the command vessels, and Guofan leaped clear and escaped as the fleet collapsed into chaos.

sentences.zh: 上疏請罪，詔旨寬免，謂於大局無傷也。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking to be punished; an edict graciously excused him, saying that the overall situation was unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking to be punished; the throne graciously excused him, declaring that the overall campaign was unharmed.

sentences.zh: 五年，賊再陷武漢，擾荊襄。

translations.literal: In the fifth year (1855), the rebels again took Wuhan and harassed Jing and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1855) the rebels again seized Wuhan and raided the Jing-Xiang region.

sentences.zh: 國籓遣胡林翼等軍還援湖北，塔齊布留攻九江，而躬至南昌撫定水師之困內湖者。

translations.literal: Guofan sent Hu Linyi and others back to aid Hubei, left Taqibu to besiege Jiujiang, and went in person to Nanchang to reassure the river force trapped in the inner lake.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan sent Hu Linyi and others back to relieve Hubei, left Taqibu to press the siege of Jiujiang, and went in person to Nanchang to steady the fleet trapped in Poyang Lake.

sentences.zh: 澤南從征江西，复弋陽，拔廣信，破義寧，而塔齊布卒於軍。

translations.literal: Zinan campaigned in Jiangxi, recovered Yiyang, took Guangxin, broke Yining, while Taqibu died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Zinan campaigned in Jiangxi, retaking Yiyang, capturing Guangxin, and breaking Yining, while Taqibu died in camp.

sentences.zh: 國籓在江西與巡撫陳啟邁不相能，澤南奔命往來，上書國籓，言東南大勢在武昌，請率所部援鄂，國籓從之。

translations.literal: Guofan in Jiangxi did not get along with Governor Chen Qimai; Zinan rushed back and forth on urgent orders and wrote to Guofan that the great strategic point of the southeast lay at Wuchang, asking to lead his troops to aid Hubei; Guofan agreed.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangxi Guofan clashed with Governor Chen Qimai; Luo Zinan shuttled back and forth on urgent orders and wrote to Guofan that the key to the southeast was Wuchang, asking to lead his division to relieve Hubei, and Guofan agreed.

sentences.zh: 幕客劉蓉諫曰：「公所恃者塔、羅。

translations.literal: Staff member Liu Rong remonstrated: "What Your Excellency relies on are Ta and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: His adviser Liu Rong objected: "You rely on Taqibu and Luo Zinan.

sentences.zh: 今塔將軍亡，羅又遠行，脫有急，誰堪使者？

translations.literal: Now General Ta is dead and Luo has gone far away; if there is an emergency, who can be sent?
translations.idiomatic: Taqibu is dead and Luo is marching away—if trouble comes, who will you send?

sentences.zh: 」國籓曰：「吾計之熟矣，東南大局宜如是，俱困於此無為也。

translations.literal: " Guofan said: "I have thought this through thoroughly; the overall situation of the southeast should be handled thus—if we are all trapped here it accomplishes nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan replied, "I have weighed this carefully. The southeast must be handled this way—we accomplish nothing if we all stay trapped here.

sentences.zh: 」嵩燾祖餞澤南曰：「曾公兵單，奈何？

translations.literal: " At the farewell feast Songsong said to Zinan: "Lord Zeng's forces are few—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: At the farewell feast Guo Songsong said to Luo Zinan, "Lord Zeng's force is thin—what then?

sentences.zh: 」澤南曰：「天苟不亡本朝，公必不死。

translations.literal: " Zinan said: "If Heaven does not wish this dynasty to perish, Lord Zeng surely will not die.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Zinan answered, "If Heaven does not mean to destroy our dynasty, Lord Zeng will not die.

sentences.zh: 」九月，補授兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: " In the ninth month he was formally appointed Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he received formal appointment as Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 六年，賊酋石達開由湖北竄江西，連陷八府一州，九江賊踞自如，湖南北聲息不相聞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year (1856), the rebel chief Shi Dakai fled from Hubei into Jiangxi and in succession took eight prefectures and one department; the rebels at Jiujiang held their ground as before, and north and south of Hunan no word of each other could be heard.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1856) the rebel leader Shi Dakai swept from Hubei into Jiangxi and seized eight prefectures and one department in succession; the rebels at Jiujiang held firm as ever, and Hunan was cut off from news north and south.

sentences.zh: 國籓困南昌，遣將分屯要地，羽檄交馳，不廢吟誦。

translations.literal: Guofan was besieged at Nanchang, sent generals to garrison key points, and urgent dispatches flew back and forth, yet he did not abandon recitation and chanting.
translations.idiomatic: Besieged at Nanchang, Guofan posted generals at key points; urgent dispatches flew back and forth, yet he never set aside his daily reading and recitation.

sentences.zh: 作水陸師得勝歌，教軍士戰守技藝、結營布陳之法，歌者咸感奮，以殺賊敢死為榮。

translations.literal: He composed victory songs for the land and river forces, teaching the soldiers techniques of attack and defense and methods of encamping and deploying formations; those who sang were all stirred and took it as glory to kill rebels and dare death.
translations.idiomatic: He composed victory songs for the army and fleet, using them to teach tactics of attack and defense and methods of camp layout and battle formation; the men who sang them were stirred to fervor and took pride in killing rebels and facing death without fear.

sentences.zh: 顧眾寡，終不能大挫賊。

translations.literal: Yet considering the disparity of numbers, in the end he could not inflict a major blow on the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Given his numbers, however, he could never deliver a decisive blow to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 議者爭請調澤南軍，上以武漢功垂成，不可棄。

translations.literal: Critics all urged that Zinan's army be transferred; the emperor held that the Wuhan campaign was near success and could not be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Critics clamored to recall Luo Zinan's army, but the emperor ruled that the Wuhan campaign was near success and must not be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 澤南督戰益急，卒死於軍。

translations.literal: Zinan pressed the fighting ever harder and in the end died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Zinan pressed the fighting ever harder and in the end died in the field.

sentences.zh: 玉麟聞江西警，芒鞋走千里，穿賊中至南昌助守。

translations.literal: Yulin, hearing the alarm in Jiangxi, walked a thousand li in straw sandals, passed through the midst of the rebels, and reached Nanchang to help in the defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Peng Yulin heard the alarm in Jiangxi, he walked a thousand li in straw sandals, passed through enemy lines, and reached Nanchang to help hold the city.

sentences.zh: 林翼已為湖北巡撫，國籓弟國華、國葆用父命乞師林翼，將五千人攻瑞州。

translations.literal: Linyi was already Governor of Hubei; Guofan's younger brothers Guohua and Guobao, invoking their father's command, begged troops from Linyi and led five thousand men to attack Ruizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi was now Governor of Hubei; Guofan's brothers Guohua and Guobao, invoking their father's order, begged troops from Hu Linyi and led five thousand men against Ruizhou.

sentences.zh: 湖南巡撫駱秉章亦資國荃兵援吉安，兄弟皆會行間。

translations.literal: Hunan Governor Luo Bingzhang also supplied Guoquan's troops to relieve Ji'an, and the brothers all met in the field.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan Governor Luo Bingzhang also supplied Zeng Guoquan's troops to relieve Ji'an, and the brothers all served together in the field.

sentences.zh: 而國籓前所遣援湖北諸軍，久之再克武漢，直下九江，李續賓八千人軍城東。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the forces Guofan had earlier sent to aid Hubei, after a long interval, again took Wuhan and drove straight down to Jiujiang; Li Xubing with eight thousand men encamped east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the forces Guofan had sent to relieve Hubei, after a long campaign, retook Wuhan and drove down to Jiujiang, where Li Xubing encamped eight thousand men east of the city.

sentences.zh: 續賓者，與弟續宜皆澤南高第弟子也。

translations.literal: Xubing and his younger brother Xuyi were both outstanding disciples of Zinan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xubing and his younger brother Li Xuyi were both among Luo Zinan's finest pupils.

sentences.zh: 載福戰船四百泊江兩岸，江寧將軍都興阿馬隊、鮑超步隊駐小池口，凡數万人。

translations.literal: Zaifu moored four hundred warships along both banks of the river; the Manchu garrison general of Jiangning, Duxing'a, with his cavalry, and Bao Chao's infantry were stationed at Xiaochikou—in all tens of thousands of men.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaifu anchored four hundred warships along both banks; the Jiangning garrison general Duxing'a with his cavalry and Bao Chao's infantry held Xiaochikou—in all tens of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 國籓本以憂懼治軍，自南昌迎勞，見軍容甚盛，益申儆告誡之。

translations.literal: Guofan had governed the army through anxiety and fear; he went out from Nanchang to welcome and encourage them, saw the troops in great array, and all the more delivered stern warnings and admonitions.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan had always led his army through anxiety and strict discipline; he came out from Nanchang to welcome them, saw their imposing array, and redoubled his stern warnings and admonitions.

sentences.zh: 而是時江南大營潰，督師向榮退守丹陽，卒。

translations.literal: Yet at this time the Great Camp of Jiangnan collapsed; the commanding general Xiang Rong withdrew to defend Danyang and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at that very moment the Great Camp of Jiangnan collapsed; Commander Xiang Rong fell back to Danyang and died there.

sentences.zh: 和春為欽差大臣，張國樑總統諸軍攻江寧。

translations.literal: He Chun served as Imperial Commissioner, and Zhang Guoliang commanded all armies in the attack on Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun was appointed Imperial Commissioner, and Zhang Guoliang took overall command of the armies attacking Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，國籓聞父憂，迳歸。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year of Xianfeng, Zeng Guofan heard of his father's death and returned home directly.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year of Xianfeng, Zeng Guofan learned of his father's death and returned home at once.

sentences.zh: 給三月假治喪，堅請終制，允開侍郎缺。

translations.literal: He was granted three months' leave for mourning but insisted on completing the full mourning period; the court allowed him to vacate his vice-ministerial post.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted three months' leave to mourn but insisted on observing the full mourning term; the court permitted him to relinquish his vice-ministership.

sentences.zh: 林翼既定湖北，進圍九江，破湖口，水師絕數年復合。

translations.literal: After Hu Linyi had pacified Hubei, he advanced to besiege Jiujiang, took Hukou, and after years of separation the river fleet was reunited.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hu Linyi had secured Hubei, he pressed the siege of Jiujiang, broke Hukou, and after years cut off the river fleet was reunited.

sentences.zh: 載福連拔望江、東流，揚風過安慶，克銅陵泥汊，與江南軍通。

translations.literal: Yang Zaifu took Wangjiang and Dongliu in succession, swept past Anqing, captured Tongling and Nizha, and linked up with the Jiangnan forces.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaifu captured Wangjiang and Dongliu in succession, swept past Anqing, took Tongling and Nizha, and joined the Jiangnan army.

sentences.zh: 由是湘軍水師名天下。

translations.literal: From this the Hunan Army's river fleet gained renown throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: From this the Hunan Army's river fleet won fame throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 林翼以此軍創始國籓，楊、彭皆其舊部，請起國籓視師。

translations.literal: Hu Linyi, noting that Zeng Guofan had founded this army and that Yang and Peng were both his old subordinates, petitioned that Zeng Guofan be recalled to oversee the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi, pointing out that Zeng Guofan had created this army and that Yang Zaifu and Peng Yulin were both his old officers, asked that Zeng Guofan be recalled to command the forces.

sentences.zh: 會九江克復，石達開竄浙江，浸及福建，分股复犯江西，朝旨詔國籓出辦浙江軍務。

translations.literal: Just as Jiujiang was recovered, Shi Dakai fled into Zhejiang, gradually reaching Fujian; a detached force again invaded Jiangxi, and an imperial edict ordered Zeng Guofan out to manage Zhejiang military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Jiujiang was retaken, Shi Dakai fled into Zhejiang and gradually into Fujian, while a splinter force again raided Jiangxi; the court ordered Zeng Guofan to take charge of Zhejiang military affairs.

sentences.zh: 國籓至江西，屯建昌，又詔援閩。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan reached Jiangxi and encamped at Jianchang; he was then ordered to aid Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan reached Jiangxi and encamped at Jianchang, and was then ordered to relieve Fujian.

sentences.zh: 國籓以閩賊不足慮，而景德地衝要，遣將援贛北，攻景德。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan judged the Fujian rebels no great concern, but Jingdezhen lay at a strategic crossroads; he sent generals to aid northern Ganzhou and attack Jingdezhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan thought the Fujian rebels were not the main worry, but Jingdezhen stood at a vital junction; he sent generals to aid northern Ganzhou and attack Jingdezhen.

sentences.zh: 國荃追賊至浮梁，江西列城次第复。

translations.literal: Zeng Guoquan pursued the rebels to Fuliang, and the cities of Jiangxi were recovered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guoquan pursued the rebels to Fuliang, and the cities of Jiangxi were retaken in succession.

sentences.zh: 時石達開復竄湖南，圍寶慶。

translations.literal: At this time Shi Dakai again fled into Hunan and besieged Shaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Shi Dakai again fled into Hunan and besieged Shaoyang.

sentences.zh: 上慮四川且有變，林翼亦以湖北餉倚川鹽，而國籓又久治兵，無疆寄，乃與官文合疏請國籓援蜀。

translations.literal: The emperor feared trouble might also arise in Sichuan; Hu Linyi noted that Hubei's supplies depended on Sichuan salt, and Zeng Guofan, long engaged in military affairs, held no territorial appointment—together with Guan Wen he jointly memorialized asking that Zeng Guofan be sent to aid Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared Sichuan might also be unsettled; Hu Linyi argued that Hubei's supplies depended on Sichuan salt, and that Zeng Guofan, long at war, held no territorial post—he and Guan Wen jointly memorialized asking that Zeng Guofan be sent to relieve Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 會賊竄廣西，上游兵事解，而陳玉成再破廬州，續賓戰歿三河，林翼以群盜蔓廬、壽間，終為楚患，乃改議留國籓合謀皖。

translations.literal: When the rebels fled into Guangxi and upstream military affairs eased, Chen Yucheng again took Luzhou and Li Xubing fell in battle at Sanhe; Hu Linyi, seeing bandits spreading between Luzhou and Shouzhou and ultimately threatening Chu, changed the proposal and urged keeping Zeng Guofan to plan jointly against Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels fled into Guangxi and eased pressure upstream, Chen Yucheng again seized Luzhou and Li Xubing was killed at Sanhe; Hu Linyi, seeing bandits spreading between Luzhou and Shouzhou and ultimately threatening Hunan, changed course and urged keeping Zeng Guofan to plan the Anhui campaign together.

sentences.zh: 軍分三道，各萬人。

translations.literal: The army was divided into three columns of ten thousand men each.
translations.idiomatic: The army was split into three columns of ten thousand men each.

sentences.zh: 國籓由宿松、石牌規安慶，多隆阿、鮑超出太湖取桐城，林翼自英山鄉舒、六。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan moved from Susong and Shipai toward Anqing; Duolonga and Bao Chao crossed Lake Tai to take Tongcheng; Hu Linyi marched from Yingshan toward Shu and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan advanced from Susong and Shipai toward Anqing; Duolonga and Bao Chao crossed Lake Tai to seize Tongcheng; Hu Linyi marched from Yingshan toward Shucheng and Lu'an.

sentences.zh: 多隆阿等既大破賊小池，复太湖、潛山，遂軍桐城。

translations.literal: After Duolonga and the others inflicted a great defeat on the rebels at Xiaochi, recovered Taihu and Qianshan, they then encamped at Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Duolonga and his colleagues routed the rebels at Xiaochi and retook Taihu and Qianshan, they encamped at Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 國荃率諸軍圍安慶，與桐城軍相犄角。

translations.literal: Zeng Guoquan led the armies in besieging Anqing, mutually supporting the Tongcheng force in a pincer.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guoquan led the armies in besieging Anqing, forming a pincer with the Tongcheng force.

sentences.zh: 安慶未及下，而皖南賊陷廣德，襲破杭州。

translations.literal: Before Anqing could be taken, rebels in southern Anhui took Guangde and stormed Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before Anqing fell, rebels in southern Anhui seized Guangde and stormed Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 李秀成大會群賊建平，分道援江寧，江南大營复潰，常州、蘇州相繼失，咸豐十年閏三月也。

translations.literal: Li Xiucheng assembled the rebel hosts at Jianping and sent columns to relieve Jiangning; the Great Camp of Jiangnan collapsed again, and Changzhou and Suzhou fell in succession—it was the intercalary third month of the tenth year of Xianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiucheng gathered the rebel hosts at Jianping and sent columns to relieve Jiangning; the Great Camp of Jiangnan collapsed again, and Changzhou and Suzhou fell in turn—it was the intercalary third month of the tenth year of Xianfeng.

sentences.zh: 左宗棠聞而歎曰：「此勝敗之轉機也！

translations.literal: When Zuo Zongtang heard this he sighed and said, "This is the turning point between victory and defeat!
translations.idiomatic: When Zuo Zongtang heard the news he sighed and said, "This is the turning point between victory and defeat!

sentences.zh: 江南諸軍，將蹇兵疲久矣。

translations.literal: The armies of Jiangnan have long been led by worn-out generals with exhausted troops.
translations.idiomatic: The armies of Jiangnan have long been led by failing generals with exhausted troops.

sentences.zh: 滌而清之，庶幾後來可藉手乎？

translations.literal: If they are washed clean, perhaps those who come after may build on them?
translations.idiomatic: If they are cleared away and renewed, perhaps those who come after may have something to build on?

sentences.zh: 」或問：「誰可當者？

translations.literal: " Someone asked, "Who can take command?
translations.idiomatic: " Someone asked, "Who can take command?

sentences.zh: 」林翼曰：「朝廷以江南事付曾公，天下不足平也。

translations.literal: " Hu Linyi said, "If the court entrusts the affairs of Jiangnan to Lord Zeng, pacifying the empire will not be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: " Hu Linyi said, "If the court entrusts the affairs of Jiangnan to Lord Zeng, the whole realm can be pacified.

sentences.zh: 」於是天子慎選帥，就加國籓兵部尚書銜，署理兩江總督，旋即真，授欽差大臣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the emperor carefully chose a commander, immediately added Zeng Guofan to the Ministry of War with ministerial rank, made him acting Governor-General of the Two Jiangs, soon confirmed him in the post, and appointed him Imperial Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the emperor carefully chose a commander, immediately added Zeng Guofan to the Ministry of War with ministerial rank, made him acting Governor-General of the Two Jiangs, soon confirmed him in office, and appointed him Imperial Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是時江、浙賊氛熾，或請撤安慶圍先所急。

translations.literal: At this time rebel strength blazed in Jiangsu and Zhejiang; some urged lifting the siege of Anqing to relieve the more urgent front.
translations.idiomatic: At this time rebel strength flared in Jiangsu and Zhejiang, and some urged lifting the siege of Anqing to meet the more urgent crisis.

sentences.zh: 國籓曰：「安慶一軍為克金陵張本，不可動也。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan said, "The Anqing army is the foundation for taking Jinling; it must not be moved.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan said, "The Anqing army is the foundation for taking Jinling; it must not be moved.

sentences.zh: 」遂南渡江，駐祁門。

translations.literal: " He then crossed the Yangtze southward and encamped at Qimen.
translations.idiomatic: " He then crossed the Yangtze southward and encamped at Qimen.

sentences.zh: 江、浙官紳告急書日數十至，援蘇、援滬、援皖、援鎮江詔書亦疊下。

translations.literal: Pleas for help from officials and gentry of Jiangsu and Zhejiang arrived by the dozen each day, and edicts to aid Suzhou, Shanghai, Anhui, and Zhenjiang came down in quick succession.
translations.idiomatic: Pleas for help from Jiangsu and Zhejiang officials and gentry arrived by the dozen each day, and edicts to relieve Suzhou, Shanghai, Anhui, and Zhenjiang followed one after another.

sentences.zh: 國籓至祁門未數日，賊陷寧國，陷徽州。

translations.literal: Within days of Zeng Guofan's arrival at Qimen, the rebels took Ningguo and Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Within days of Zeng Guofan's arrival at Qimen, the rebels seized Ningguo and Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 東南方困兵革，而英吉利复失好，以兵至。

translations.literal: The southeast was battered by war, and Britain again broke relations and sent troops.
translations.idiomatic: The southeast was worn down by war, and Britain again broke relations and sent troops.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁敗績天津，文宗狩熱河，國籓聞警，請提兵北上，會和議成，乃止。

translations.literal: Sengge Rinchen was defeated at Tianjin; Emperor Xianfeng fled to Rehe; Zeng Guofan, hearing the alarm, asked to lead troops north, but when peace was negotiated he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Sengge Rinchen was defeated at Tianjin; Emperor Xianfeng fled to Rehe; Zeng Guofan, hearing the alarm, asked to march north with his army, but when peace was made he desisted.

sentences.zh: 其冬，大為賊困，一出祁門東陷婺源；

translations.literal: That winter he was greatly beset by rebels: one column east of Qimen took Wuyuan;
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was hard pressed by rebels: one column east of Qimen seized Wuyuan;

sentences.zh: 一出祁門西陷景德；

translations.literal: one west of Qimen took Jingdezhen;
translations.idiomatic: one west of Qimen seized Jingdezhen;

sentences.zh: 一入羊棧嶺攻大營。

translations.literal: one entered Yangzhan Pass and attacked the main camp.
translations.idiomatic: one entered Yangzhan Pass and attacked the main camp.

sentences.zh: 軍報絕不通，將吏惵然有憂色，固請移營江乾就水師。

translations.literal: Military reports ceased entirely; officers and officials looked fearful and repeatedly urged moving the camp to the riverbank to join the fleet.
translations.idiomatic: Military reports ceased entirely; officers and officials looked fearful and repeatedly urged moving the camp to the riverbank to join the fleet.

sentences.zh: 國籓曰：「無故退軍，兵家所忌。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan said, "A withdrawal without cause is what strategists most dread.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan said, "A withdrawal without cause is what strategists most dread.

sentences.zh: 」卒不從，使人間行檄鮑超、張運蘭亟引兵會。

translations.literal: " He would not agree, and sent men by secret routes to order Bao Chao and Zhang Yunlan to march to join him at once.
translations.idiomatic: " He refused, and sent men by secret routes to order Bao Chao and Zhang Yunlan to march to join him at once.

sentences.zh: 身在軍中，意氣自如，時與賓佐酌酒論文。

translations.literal: Though in the midst of the army, his spirits remained steady, and he sometimes drank and discussed literature with his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Though in the midst of the army, his spirits remained steady, and he sometimes drank and discussed literature with his advisers.

sentences.zh: 自官京朝，即日記所言行，後履危困無稍間。

translations.literal: Since his days at court he had kept a daily record of words and deeds, and afterward, even amid peril and hardship, he never missed a day.
translations.idiomatic: Since his days at court he had kept a daily record of words and deeds, and afterward, even amid peril and hardship, he never missed a day.

sentences.zh: 國籓駐祁門，本資餉江西，及景德失，議者爭言取徽州通浙米。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan at Qimen had originally relied on Jiangxi for supplies; when Jingdezhen fell, debaters all urged taking Huizhou to open a route for Zhejiang grain.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan at Qimen had originally drawn supplies from Jiangxi; when Jingdezhen fell, debaters all urged taking Huizhou to open a route for Zhejiang grain.

sentences.zh: 乃自將大軍次休寧，值天雨，八營皆潰，草遺囑寄家，誓死守休寧。

translations.literal: He then led the main army to Xiuning; rain fell, eight camps collapsed, he drafted a final testament to send home, and swore to hold Xiuning to the death.
translations.idiomatic: He then led the main army to Xiuning; rain fell, eight camps collapsed, he drafted a final testament to send home, and swore to hold Xiuning to the death.

sentences.zh: 適宗棠大破賊樂平，運道通，移駐東流。

translations.literal: Just then Zuo Zongtang routed the rebels at Leping, the supply route opened, and he moved his headquarters to Dongliu.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Zuo Zongtang routed the rebels at Leping, the supply route opened, and he moved his headquarters to Dongliu.

sentences.zh: 多隆阿連敗賊桐城，鮑超一軍游擊無定居，林翼復遣將助之。

translations.literal: Duolonga repeatedly defeated the rebels at Tongcheng; Bao Chao's division raided without fixed base; Hu Linyi again sent generals to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Duolonga repeatedly defeated the rebels at Tongcheng; Bao Chao's division raided without a fixed base; Hu Linyi again sent generals to assist.

sentences.zh: 十一年八月，國荃遂克安慶。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the eleventh year of Xianfeng, Zeng Guoquan at last took Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the eleventh year of Xianfeng, Zeng Guoquan at last took Anqing.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，而文宗崩，林翼亦卒。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, Emperor Xianfeng died and Hu Linyi also passed away.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, Emperor Xianfeng died and Hu Linyi also passed away.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，太后垂簾聽政，加國籓太子少保銜，命節制江蘇、安徽、江西、浙江四省。

translations.literal: Emperor Tongzhi succeeded; the Empress Dowager governed from behind the curtain; Zeng Guofan was given the rank of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and ordered to coordinate Jiangsu, Anhui, Jiangxi, and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Tongzhi succeeded; the Empress Dowager governed from behind the curtain; Zeng Guofan was given the rank of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and ordered to coordinate Jiangsu, Anhui, Jiangxi, and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 國籓惶懼，疏辭，不允，朝有大政，諮而後行。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan was fearful and memorialized to decline; the request was denied; on major state affairs he consulted the throne before acting.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan was fearful and memorialized to decline; the request was denied; on major state affairs he consulted the throne before acting.

sentences.zh: 當是時，偽天王洪秀全僭號踞金陵，偽忠王李秀成等犯蘇、滬，偽侍王李世賢等陷浙杭，偽輔王楊輔清等屯寧國，偽康王汪海洋窺江西，偽英王陳玉成屯廬州，捻首苗霈霖出入潁、壽，與玉成合，圖竄山東、河南，眾皆號數十萬。

translations.literal: At that time the false Heavenly King Hong Xiuquan held Jinling in regal pretension; the false Loyal King Li Xiucheng and others attacked Suzhou and Shanghai; the false Attendant King Li Shixian and others took Zhejiang and Hangzhou; the false Assistant King Yang Fuqing and others held Ningguo; the false King of Kang Wang Haiyang watched Jiangxi; the false Brave King Chen Yucheng held Luzhou; Nian chief Miao Peilin moved in and out of Ying and Shou, cooperating with Yucheng and plotting to break into Shandong and Henan—all numbering in the hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the false Heavenly King Hong Xiuquan held Jinling in regal pretension; the false Loyal King Li Xiucheng and others attacked Suzhou and Shanghai; the false Attendant King Li Shixian and others seized Zhejiang and Hangzhou; the false Assistant King Yang Fuqing and others held Ningguo; the false King of Kang Wang Haiyang watched Jiangxi; the false Brave King Chen Yucheng held Luzhou; Nian chief Miao Peilin moved in and out of Ying and Shou, cooperating with Yucheng and plotting to break into Shandong and Henan—all claiming forces in the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 國籓與國荃策進取，國荃曰：「急搗金陵，則寇必以全力護巢穴，而後蘇、杭可圖也。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan and Zeng Guoquan planned the advance; Guoquan said, "Strike Jinling at once, and the rebels must commit their full strength to defending their nest—then Suzhou and Hangzhou may be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan and Zeng Guoquan planned the advance; Guoquan said, "Strike Jinling at once, and the rebels must commit their full strength to defending their nest—then Suzhou and Hangzhou may be taken.

sentences.zh: 」國籓然之。

translations.literal: " Zeng Guofan agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Zeng Guofan agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃以江寧事付國荃，以浙江事付宗棠，而以江蘇事付李鴻章。

translations.literal: He entrusted affairs of Jiangning to Guoquan, affairs of Zhejiang to Zongtang, and affairs of Jiangsu to Li Hongzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted affairs of Jiangning to Guoquan, affairs of Zhejiang to Zuo Zongtang, and affairs of Jiangsu to Li Hongzhang.

sentences.zh: 鴻章故出國籓門，以編修為幕僚，改道員，至是令從淮上募勇八千，選良將付之，號「淮軍」。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang had formerly been a pupil of Zeng Guofan, served as a compiler on his staff, was transferred to circuit intendant rank, and was now ordered to raise eight thousand braves along the Huai, given fine generals, and styled the "Huai Army."
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang had formerly been Zeng Guofan's pupil, served as a compiler on his staff, was transferred to circuit intendant rank, and was now ordered to raise eight thousand braves along the Huai, given capable generals, and styled the "Huai Army."

sentences.zh: 同治元年，拜協辦大學士，督諸軍進討。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was appointed Associate Grand Secretary and directed all armies in the advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he was appointed Associate Grand Secretary and directed all armies in the advance.

sentences.zh: 於是國荃有搗金陵之師，鴻章有徵蘇、滬之師，載福、玉麟有肅清下游之師；

translations.literal: Thus Guoquan had an army to strike Jinling, Hongzhang an army to recover Suzhou and Shanghai, and Zaifu and Yulin an army to clear the lower reaches;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zeng Guoquan had an army to strike Jinling, Li Hongzhang an army to recover Suzhou and Shanghai, and Yang Zaifu and Peng Yulin an army to clear the lower reaches;

sentences.zh: 大江以北，多隆阿有取廬州之師，續宜有援潁州之師；

translations.literal: north of the Great River, Duolonga had an army to take Luzhou and Xuyi an army to aid Yingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: north of the Yangtze, Duolonga had an army to take Luzhou and Li Xuyi an army to relieve Yingzhou;

sentences.zh: 大江以南，鮑超有攻寧國之師，運蘭有防剿徽州之師，宗棠有規復全浙之師：十道並出，皆受成於國籓。

translations.literal: south of the Great River, Bao Chao had an army to attack Ningguo, Yunlan an army to defend and suppress Huizhou, and Zongtang an army to recover all Zhejiang: ten columns marched together, all operating under Zeng Guofan's authority.
translations.idiomatic: south of the Yangtze, Bao Chao had an army to attack Ningguo, Zhang Yunlan an army to defend and suppress Huizhou, and Zuo Zongtang an army to recover all Zhejiang: ten columns marched together, all operating under Zeng Guofan's authority.

sentences.zh: 賊之都金陵也，堅築壕壘，餉械足，猝不可拔。

translations.literal: As the rebels held Jinling, they had built strong ramparts and ditches with ample supplies and arms—not to be taken in a rush.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels held Jinling, they had built strong ramparts and ditches with ample supplies and arms—not to be taken in a rush.

sentences.zh: 疾疫大作，將士死亡山積，幾不能軍。

translations.literal: Plague broke out on a vast scale; officers and men died in heaps until the army could scarcely hold together.
translations.idiomatic: Plague broke out on a vast scale; officers and men died in heaps until the army could scarcely hold together.

sentences.zh: 國籓自以德薄，請簡大臣馳赴軍，俾分己責，上優詔慰勉之，謂：「天災流行，豈卿一人之咎？

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan, judging his own virtue insufficient, asked that a senior minister be sent to the army to share his responsibility; the throne issued a gracious edict of consolation and encouragement, saying, "When calamity spreads from Heaven, how can the fault be yours alone?
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan, judging his own virtue insufficient, asked that a senior minister be sent to the army to share his burden; the throne issued a gracious edict of consolation, saying, "When calamity spreads from Heaven, how can the fault be yours alone?

sentences.zh: 意者朝廷政多缺失，我君臣當勉圖禳救，為民請命。

translations.literal: Perhaps the court's policies have many failings; we ruler and ministers should strive to avert disaster and plead for the people's lives.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps the court's policies have many failings; we ruler and ministers should strive to avert disaster and plead for the people's lives.

sentences.zh: 且環顧中外，才力、氣量無逾卿者！

translations.literal: Moreover, looking all around at home and abroad, none surpass you in talent, strength, and breadth of mind!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, looking all around at home and abroad, none surpass you in talent, strength, and breadth of mind!

sentences.zh: 時勢艱難，無稍懈也。

translations.literal: The times are hard; do not slacken in the least.
translations.idiomatic: The times are hard; do not slacken in the least.

sentences.zh: 」國籓讀詔感泣。

translations.literal: " Zeng Guofan read the edict and wept with emotion.
translations.idiomatic: " Zeng Guofan read the edict and wept with emotion.

sentences.zh: 時洪秀全被圍久，召李秀成蘇州，李世賢浙江，悉眾來援，號六十萬，圍雨花台軍。

translations.literal: At this time Hong Xiuquan, long besieged, summoned Li Xiucheng from Suzhou and Li Shixian from Zhejiang; they came with all their forces, claiming six hundred thousand men, and besieged the army at Yuhuatai.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Hong Xiuquan, long besieged, summoned Li Xiucheng from Suzhou and Li Shixian from Zhejiang; they came with all their forces, claiming six hundred thousand men, and besieged the army at Yuhuatai.

sentences.zh: 國荃拒戰六十四日，解去。

translations.literal: Guoquan resisted for sixty-four days, and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guoquan resisted for sixty-four days, and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，水師克九洑洲，江寧城合圍。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Tongzhi, the river fleet took Jiufuzhou and Jiangning was completely encircled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year of Tongzhi, the river fleet took Jiufuzhou and Jiangning was completely encircled.

sentences.zh: 十月，鴻章克蘇州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Hongzhang took Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Li Hongzhang took Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，宗棠克杭州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year of Tongzhi, Zongtang took Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year of Tongzhi, Zuo Zongtang took Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 國籓以江寧久不下，請鴻章來會師，未發，國荃攻益急，克之。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan, because Jiangning would not fall, asked Hongzhang to come for a joint campaign; before he set out, Guoquan pressed the attack ever harder and took the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan, because Jiangning would not fall, asked Li Hongzhang to come for a joint campaign; before he set out, Zeng Guoquan pressed the attack ever harder and took the city.

sentences.zh: 江寧平，天子褒功，加太子太傅，封一等毅勇侯，賞雙眼翎。

translations.literal: With Jiangning pacified, the emperor rewarded merit: Zeng Guofan was made Senior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed as First-rank Marquis of Yiyong with brave merit, and granted the double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: With Jiangning pacified, the emperor rewarded merit: Zeng Guofan was made Senior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed as First-rank Marquis of Yiyong with brave merit, and granted the double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 開國以來，文臣封侯自是始。

translations.literal: Since the founding of the dynasty, this was the first enfeoffment of a civil official as marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of the dynasty, this was the first enfeoffment of a civil official as marquis.

sentences.zh: 朝野稱賀，而國籓功成不居，粥粥如畏。

translations.literal: Court and country celebrated, yet Zeng Guofan, his work complete, did not presume; he remained cautious and deferential as if in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country celebrated, yet Zeng Guofan, his work complete, did not presume; he remained cautious and deferential as if in fear.

sentences.zh: 穆宗每簡督撫，輒密詢其人，未敢指缺疏薦，以謂疆臣既專征伐，不當更分黜陟之柄，外重內輕之漸，不可不防。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Tongzhi chose governors and governors-general, he secretly inquired about the man; Zeng Guofan dared not nominate by name in memorials, holding that frontier commanders already wielded punitive authority and should not also share appointment and dismissal power—the drift toward external strength and internal weakness must be guarded against.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Tongzhi chose governors and governors-general, he secretly inquired about the man; Zeng Guofan dared not nominate by name in memorials, holding that frontier commanders already wielded punitive authority and should not also share appointment and dismissal power—the drift toward external strength and internal weakness must be guarded against.

sentences.zh: 初，官軍積習深，勝不讓，敗不救。

translations.literal: At first, government armies were deeply set in bad habits: victors would not yield credit, the defeated would not rescue one another.
translations.idiomatic: At first, government armies were deeply set in bad habits: victors would not yield credit, the defeated would not rescue one another.

sentences.zh: 國籓練湘軍，謂必萬眾一心，乃可辦賊，故以忠誠倡天下。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan trained the Hunan Army, holding that only when ten thousand men were of one mind could rebels be subdued, and so he took loyalty and integrity as his banner to the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan trained the Hunan Army, holding that only when ten thousand men were of one mind could rebels be subdued, and so he took loyalty and integrity as his banner to the empire.

sentences.zh: 其後又謂淮上風氣勁，宜別立一軍。

translations.literal: Later he also held that the Huai region's spirit was vigorous and a separate army should be raised.
translations.idiomatic: Later he also held that the Huai region's spirit was vigorous and a separate army should be raised.

sentences.zh: 湘勇利山徑，馳騁平原非所長，且用武十年，氣亦稍衰矣，故欲練淮士為湘勇之繼。

translations.literal: Hunan braves excelled on mountain paths but were not suited to plains campaigning; after ten years of war their ardor had slackened somewhat, so he wished to train Huai men as successors to the Hunan braves.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan braves excelled on mountain paths but were not suited to plains campaigning; after ten years of war their ardor had slackened somewhat, so he wished to train Huai men as successors to the Hunan braves.

sentences.zh: 至是東南大定，裁湘軍，進淮軍，而捻匪事起。

translations.literal: By then the southeast was largely settled; he reduced the Hunan Army and expanded the Huai Army, and the Nian bandit trouble arose.
translations.idiomatic: By then the southeast was largely settled; he reduced the Hunan Army and expanded the Huai Army, and the Nian bandit trouble arose.

sentences.zh: 捻匪者，始於山東遊民相聚，其後剽掠光、固、潁、亳、淮、徐之間，捻紙燃脂，故謂之「捻」。

translations.literal: The Nian bandits began as vagabonds gathering in Shandong; later they raided between Guang, Gu, Ying, Bo, Huai, and Xu; they twisted paper and lit fat to signal—hence the name "Nian."
translations.idiomatic: The Nian bandits began as vagabonds gathering in Shandong; later they raided between Guangde, Gushi, Yingzhou, Bozhou, Huai, and Xu; they twisted paper and lit fat to signal—hence the name "Nian."

sentences.zh: 有眾數十萬，馬數万，蹂躪數千里，分合不常。

translations.literal: They numbered hundreds of thousands, with tens of thousands of horses, trampling thousands of li, splitting and merging without fixed pattern.
translations.idiomatic: They numbered hundreds of thousands, with tens of thousands of horses, trampling thousands of li, splitting and merging without fixed pattern.

sentences.zh: 捻首四人，曰張總愚、任柱、牛洪、賴文光。

translations.literal: There were four Nian chiefs: Zhang Zongwan, Ren Zhu, Niu Hong, and Lai Wenguang.
translations.idiomatic: There were four Nian chiefs: Zhang Zongwan, Ren Zhu, Niu Hong, and Lai Wenguang.

sentences.zh: 自洪寇、苗練嘗糾捻與官軍戰，益悉攻鬥，勝保、袁甲三不能禦。

translations.literal: Since the Taiping rebels and militia leaders had often enlisted Nian bands to fight government troops, they grew ever more skilled in combat; Sheng Bao and Yuan Jiasan could not hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Taiping rebels and militia leaders had often enlisted Nian bands to fight government troops, they grew ever more skilled in combat; Sheng Bao and Yuan Jiasan could not hold them.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁征討數年，亦未能大創之。

translations.literal: Sengge Rinchen campaigned for years yet could not inflict a crushing blow.
translations.idiomatic: Sengge Rinchen campaigned for years yet could not inflict a crushing blow.

sentences.zh: 國籓聞僧軍輕騎追賊，一日夜三百餘裡，曰：「此於兵法，必蹶上將軍。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan heard that Seng's army pursued rebels with light cavalry three hundred-plus li in a day and night, and said, "By the art of war this must bring the commanding general to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan heard that Sengge Rinchen's army pursued rebels with light cavalry more than three hundred li in a day and night, and said, "By the art of war this must bring the commanding general to ruin.

sentences.zh: 」未幾而王果戰歿曹州，上聞大驚，詔國籓速赴山東剿捻，節制直隸、山東、河南三省，而鴻章代為總督，廷旨日促出師。

translations.literal: " Before long the prince indeed fell in battle at Caozhou; the emperor was greatly alarmed and ordered Zeng Guofan to hasten to Shandong to suppress the Nian, coordinate Zhili, Shandong, and Henan, while Hongzhang replaced him as governor-general; court orders daily pressed him to march.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long the prince indeed fell in battle at Caozhou; the emperor was greatly alarmed and ordered Zeng Guofan to hasten to Shandong to suppress the Nian, coordinate Zhili, Shandong, and Henan, while Li Hongzhang replaced him as governor-general; court orders daily pressed him to march.

sentences.zh: 國籓上言：「楚軍裁撤殆盡，今調劉松山一軍及劉銘傳淮勇尚不足。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan memorialized: "The Chu army has been reduced almost to nothing; even with Liu Songshen's division and Liu Mingchuan's Huai braves now mobilized, the force is still insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan memorialized: "The Chu army has been reduced almost to nothing; even with Liu Songshen's division and Liu Mingchuan's Huai braves now mobilized, the force is still insufficient.

sentences.zh: 當更募徐州勇，以楚軍之規模，開齊、兗之風氣；

translations.literal: More braves should be raised at Xuzhou, on the model of the Chu army, to develop the spirit of Qi and Yan;
translations.idiomatic: More braves should be raised at Xuzhou, on the model of the Chu army, to develop the spirit of Qi and Yan;

sentences.zh: 又增募馬隊及黃河水師，皆非旦夕可就。

translations.literal: cavalry and a Yellow River fleet should also be added—these cannot be ready overnight.
translations.idiomatic: cavalry and a Yellow River fleet should also be added—these cannot be ready overnight.

sentences.zh: 直隸宜自籌防兵，分守河岸，不宜令河南之兵兼顧河北。

translations.literal: Zhili should raise its own defensive troops and garrison the riverbanks; Henan's army should not be made to cover Hebei as well.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili should raise its own defensive troops and garrison the riverbanks; Henan's army should not be made to cover Hebei as well.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁嘗週曆五省，臣不能也。

translations.literal: Sengge Rinchen once toured five provinces; your servant cannot do that.
translations.idiomatic: Sengge Rinchen once toured five provinces; your servant cannot do that.

sentences.zh: 如以徐州為老營，則山東之兗、沂、曹、濟，河南之歸、陳，江甦之淮、徐、海，安徽之廬、鳳、潁、泗，此十三府州責之臣，而以其餘責各督撫。

translations.literal: If Xuzhou is made the base camp, then Yan, Yi, Cao, and Ji in Shandong; Gui and Chen in Henan; Huai, Xu, and Hai in Jiangsu; and Lu, Feng, Ying, and Si in Anhui—these thirteen prefectures and departments would be my responsibility, and the rest would fall to the various governors and governors-general.
translations.idiomatic: If Xuzhou is made the base camp, then Yan, Yi, Cao, and Ji in Shandong; Gui and Chen in Henan; Huai, Xu, and Hai in Jiangsu; and Lu, Feng, Ying, and Si in Anhui—these thirteen prefectures and departments would be my responsibility, and the rest would fall to the various governors and governors-general.

sentences.zh: 汛地有專屬，則軍務乃漸有歸宿。

translations.literal: When garrison districts have fixed assignments, military affairs gradually find their proper place.
translations.idiomatic: When garrison districts have fixed assignments, military affairs gradually find their proper place.

sentences.zh: 」又奏：「扼要駐軍臨淮關、周家口、濟寧、徐州，為四鎮。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized: "Troops should be stationed at key points at Linhuaiguan, Zhoujiakou, Jining, and Xuzhou as four garrison towns.
translations.idiomatic: " He also memorialized: "Troops should be stationed at key points at Linhuaiguan, Zhoujiakou, Jining, and Xuzhou as four garrison towns.

sentences.zh: 一處有急，三處往援。

translations.literal: When one place is in crisis, three others go to its aid.
translations.idiomatic: When one place is in crisis, three others go to its aid.

sentences.zh: 今賊已成流寇，若賊流而我與之俱流，必致疲於奔命。

translations.literal: Now the rebels have become roving bandits; if they roam and we roam with them, we must wear ourselves out in endless pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Now the rebels have become roving bandits; if they roam and we roam with them, we must wear ourselves out in endless pursuit.

sentences.zh: 故臣堅持初議，以有定之兵，制無定之寇，重迎剿，不重尾追。

translations.literal: Therefore your servant holds to his original proposal: use fixed troops to control unfixed bandits, emphasizing intercepting strikes rather than trailing pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore your servant holds to his original proposal: use fixed troops to control unfixed bandits, emphasizing intercepting strikes rather than trailing pursuit.

sentences.zh: 」然督師年餘，捻馳突如故。

translations.literal: " Yet after more than a year as commanding general, the Nian still raided as before.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet after more than a year as commanding general, the Nian still raided as before.

sentences.zh: 將士皆謂不苦戰而苦奔逐，乃起張秋抵清江築長牆，憑運河御之，未成而捻竄襄、鄧間，因移而西，修沙河、賈魯河，開壕置守。

translations.literal: Officers and men all complained that their hardship lay not in fighting but in endless pursuit; he then built a long wall from Zhangqiu to Qingjiang, relying on the Grand Canal for defense; before it was finished the Nian broke into Xiang and Deng, so he shifted west, repaired the Sha and Jialu rivers, dug trenches, and set guards.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men all complained that their hardship lay not in fighting but in endless pursuit; he then built a long wall from Zhangqiu to Qingjiang, relying on the Grand Canal for defense; before it was finished the Nian broke into Xiangyang and Dengzhou, so he shifted west, repaired the Sha and Jialu rivers, dug trenches, and set guards.

sentences.zh: 分地甫定，而捻衝河南汛地，复突而東。

translations.literal: The territorial divisions had just been set when the Nian struck the Henan defense sectors and again burst eastward.
translations.idiomatic: The territorial divisions had barely been fixed when the Nian struck the Henan defense lines and surged east again.

sentences.zh: 時議頗咎國籓計迂闊，然亦無他術可制捻也。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion largely blamed Zeng Guofan's plans as impractical and broad, yet there was no other method that could control the Nian.
translations.idiomatic: Critics widely blamed Zeng Guofan's strategy as ponderous and impractical, yet no other method could bring the Nian to heel.

sentences.zh: 山東、河南民習見僧格林沁戰，皆怪國籓以督兵大臣安坐徐州，謗議盈路。

translations.literal: The people of Shandong and Henan, accustomed to seeing Sengge Rinchen fight in person, all wondered at Zeng Guofan, a commander supervising troops, sitting quietly at Xuzhou; slander filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shandong and Henan, used to Sengge Rinchen fighting in the field, resented Zeng Guofan, a commander-in-chief, sitting quietly at Xuzhou, and slander filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 國籓在軍久，益慎用兵。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan had been long in the army and grew ever more cautious in employing troops.
translations.idiomatic: After long years in the field, Zeng Guofan grew ever more cautious about committing troops.

sentences.zh: 初立駐軍四鎮之議，次設扼守黃運河之策。

translations.literal: First he established the proposal of four garrison towns; next he devised the strategy of holding the Yellow River and Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: First came his plan for four fixed garrison towns; then his strategy of holding the Yellow River and Grand Canal line.

sentences.zh: 既數為言路所劾，亦自以防河無效，朝廷方起用國荃，乃奏請鴻章以江督出駐徐州，與魯撫會辦東路；

translations.literal: Having been impeached several times by the censorate and himself finding river defense ineffective, while the court was now employing Guoquan, he memorialized asking that Hongzhang, as Jiangsu governor-general, go out to Xuzhou and jointly handle the eastern route with the Shandong governor;
translations.idiomatic: After repeated impeachment from the censorate and his own sense that river defense was failing, while the court was recalling Guoquan, he memorialized that Li Hongzhang, as governor-general of Jiangsu, should take the field at Xuzhou and jointly handle the eastern front with the Shandong governor;

sentences.zh: 國荃以鄂撫出駐襄陽，與豫撫會辦西路：而自駐周家口策應之。

translations.literal: Guoquan, as Hubei governor, would go out to Xiangyang and jointly handle the western route with the Henan governor; Zeng Guofan himself would remain at Zhoujiakou to coordinate support.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guoquan, as Hubei governor, would take the field at Xiangyang and handle the western front with the Henan governor, while Zeng Guofan himself would remain at Zhoujiakou to coordinate.

sentences.zh: 或又劾其驕妄，於是國籓念權位不可久處，益有憂讒畏譏之心矣。

translations.literal: Some again impeached him for arrogance; then Zeng Guofan reflected that high position could not be held long and grew ever more anxious about slander and fearful of ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Others impeached him for arrogance, and Zeng Guofan concluded that power could not be held indefinitely; he grew ever more wary of slander and fearful of public censure.

sentences.zh: 匈病假數月，繼請開缺，以散員留軍效力；

translations.literal: He took sick leave for several months, then asked to vacate his post and remain with the army as a man without office to serve;
translations.idiomatic: He took sick leave for several months, then asked to resign his post and remain with the army as a private citizen to serve;

sentences.zh: 又請削封爵：皆不許。

translations.literal: he also asked that his enfeoffment be stripped away: none of these requests was granted.
translations.idiomatic: he also asked to surrender his enfeoffment—all were denied.

sentences.zh: 五年冬，還任江南，而鴻章代督軍。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year of Tongzhi, he returned to his post in Jiangnan, and Hongzhang replaced him in command of the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifth year of Tongzhi he returned to Jiangnan, and Li Hongzhang took over command of the army.

sentences.zh: 時牛洪死，張總愚竄陝西，任柱、賴文光竄湖北，自是有東西捻之號。

translations.literal: At this time Niu Hong died; Zhang Zongwan fled into Shaanxi, and Ren Zhu and Lai Wenguang fled into Hubei—from this came the names Eastern and Western Nian.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong was dead; Zhang Zongwan fled into Shaanxi while Ren Zhu and Lai Wenguang fled into Hubei—from then on they were called the Eastern and Western Nian.

sentences.zh: 六年，就補大學士，留治所。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he received formal appointment as Grand Secretary and remained at his post of governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he received formal appointment as Grand Secretary and remained at his post.

sentences.zh: 東捻由河南竄登、萊、青，李鴻章、劉長佑建議合四省兵力堵運河。

translations.literal: The Eastern Nian fled from Henan into Dengzhou, Laizhou, and Qingzhou; Li Hongzhang and Liu Changyou proposed combining the forces of four provinces to block the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Nian fled from Henan into Dengzhou, Laizhou, and Qingzhou; Li Hongzhang and Liu Changyou proposed pooling four provinces' forces to block the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 賊復引而西，越膠、萊、河南入海州。

translations.literal: The bandits again drew westward, crossed Jiaozhou, Laizhou, and Henan, and entered Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits turned west again, crossed Jiaozhou, Laizhou, and Henan, and entered Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 官軍陣斬任柱，賴文光走死揚州。

translations.literal: The government army killed Ren Zhu in battle, and Lai Wenguang fled and died at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Government forces killed Ren Zhu in battle, and Lai Wenguang fled and died at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以東捻平，加國籓雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: Because the Eastern Nian were pacified, Zeng Guofan was granted the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain.
translations.idiomatic: With the Eastern Nian suppressed, Zeng Guofan was granted the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain.

sentences.zh: 西捻入陝後，為松山所敗。

translations.literal: After the Western Nian entered Shaanxi, they were defeated by Songshan.
translations.idiomatic: After the Western Nian entered Shaanxi, Liu Songshan defeated them.

sentences.zh: 乘堅冰渡河竄山西，入直隸，犯保定、天津。

translations.literal: They crossed the river on solid ice into Shanxi, entered Zhili, and attacked Baoding and Tianjin.
