translations.idiomatic: They crossed the frozen river into Shanxi, entered Zhili, and threatened Baoding and Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 松山繞出賊前，破之於獻縣。

translations.literal: Songshan circled ahead of the bandits and defeated them at Xian County.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Songshan circled ahead of them and routed them at Xian County.

sentences.zh: 諸帥勤王師大至，賊越運河竄東昌、武定。

translations.literal: The generals' armies rushing to aid the throne arrived in force; the bandits crossed the Grand Canal and fled into Dongchang and Wuding.
translations.idiomatic: Relief armies from every quarter converged, but the bandits crossed the Grand Canal and fled into Dongchang and Wuding.

sentences.zh: 鴻章移師德州，河水盛漲，扼河以困之。

translations.literal: Hongzhang moved his army to Dezhou; the river was in full flood, and he held the river line to hem them in.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang shifted his army to Dezhou; with the river in full flood, he held the line to trap them.

sentences.zh: 國籓遣黃翼升領水師助剿，大破賊於荏平。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan sent Huang Yisheng to lead the river fleet in assisting the suppression and inflicted a great defeat on the bandits at Renping.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan sent Huang Yisheng with the river fleet to assist, and government forces crushed the bandits at Renping.

sentences.zh: 張總愚赴水死，而西捻平。

translations.literal: Zhang Zongwan threw himself into the water and died, and the Western Nian were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zongwan drowned himself, and the Western Nian were suppressed.

sentences.zh: 凡防河之策，皆國籓本謀也。

translations.literal: All the strategies of river defense were originally Zeng Guofan's plans.
translations.idiomatic: Every strategy of river defense had originated with Zeng Guofan.

sentences.zh: 是年授武英殿大學士，調直隸總督。

translations.literal: That year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Eminence and transferred to Governor-General of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Eminence and transferred to Governor-General of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 國籓為政務持大體，規全勢。

translations.literal: In governing, Zeng Guofan held to the larger pattern and planned for the whole situation.
translations.idiomatic: In government Zeng Guofan held to the larger pattern and planned for the whole strategic picture.

sentences.zh: 其策西事，議先清隴寇而後出關；

translations.literal: In planning the western campaigns, he proposed first clearing the bandits of Longyou and only then advancing beyond the passes;
translations.idiomatic: For the western campaigns he proposed clearing the bandits of Longyou first and only then advancing beyond the passes;

sentences.zh: 籌滇、黔，議以蜀、湘二省為根本。

translations.literal: in planning Yunnan and Guizhou, he proposed taking the two provinces of Shu and Xiang as the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: for Yunnan and Guizhou he proposed making Sichuan and Hunan the foundation.

sentences.zh: 皆初立一議，後數年卒如其說。

translations.literal: In each case he first set forth a single proposal, and years later events finally followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: In each case he laid down a plan at the outset, and years later events vindicated him.

sentences.zh: 自西人入中國，交涉事日繁。

translations.literal: Since Westerners entered China, foreign affairs grew daily more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Once Westerners entered China, foreign affairs grew daily more pressing.

sentences.zh: 金陵未下，俄、美、英、法皆請以兵助，國籓婉拒之。

translations.literal: Before Jinling fell, Russia, America, Britain, and France all offered troops to assist; Zeng Guofan politely declined.
translations.idiomatic: Before Nanjing fell, Russia, the United States, Britain, and France all offered military aid; Zeng Guofan politely declined.

sentences.zh: 及廷議購機輪，置船械，則力贊其成，復建議選學童習藝歐洲。

translations.literal: When the court debated purchasing steam engines and establishing shipyards and arsenals, he strongly urged their success and again proposed selecting schoolboys to study crafts in Europe.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated purchasing steam engines and establishing arsenals, he strongly supported the plan and proposed selecting schoolboys to study Western technology in Europe.

sentences.zh: 每定約章，輒詔問可許不可許，國籓以為爭彼我之虛儀者可許，其奪吾民生計者勿許也。

translations.literal: Whenever treaties were drafted, edicts would ask what might be granted or refused; Zeng Guofan held that disputes over empty ceremony between us and them could be conceded, but what seized the livelihood of our people must not be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever treaties were drafted, the throne asked what might be conceded; Zeng Guofan held that empty disputes over ceremony could be yielded, but anything that threatened the people's livelihood must be refused.

sentences.zh: 既至直隸，以練兵、飭吏、治河三端為要務，次第興革，設清訟局、禮賢館，政教大行。

translations.literal: Once he reached Zhili, he made training troops, disciplining officials, and controlling the rivers the three chief tasks, carried out reforms step by step, established bureaus for clearing lawsuits and halls for honoring worthies, and government and instruction flourished widely.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Zhili he made troop training, official discipline, and river control his three priorities, carried out reforms in sequence, established bureaus for clearing lawsuits and halls for honoring worthies, and government and moral instruction flourished.

sentences.zh: 九年四月，天津民擊殺法領事豐大業，毀教堂，傷教民數十人。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the ninth year of Tongzhi, the people of Tianjin killed the French consul Fontanier, destroyed churches, and wounded dozens of Christians.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the ninth year of Tongzhi, Tianjin residents killed the French consul Fontanier, destroyed churches, and wounded dozens of Christians.

sentences.zh: 通商大臣崇厚議嚴懲之，民不服。

translations.literal: The trade commissioner Chonghou proposed severe punishment; the people would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Trade Commissioner Chonghou proposed severe punishment, but the people would not accept it.

sentences.zh: 國籓方病目，詔速赴津，乃務持平保和局，殺十七人，又遣戍府縣吏。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan was then ill in the eyes; an edict ordered him to hurry to Tianjin. He strove to be even-handed and preserve peace, executed seventeen men, and banished prefectural and district officials.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan was then suffering from eye trouble when an edict ordered him to Tianjin at once. He sought a balanced settlement to preserve peace, executed seventeen men, and banished prefectural and district officials.

sentences.zh: 國籓之初至也，津民謂必反崇厚所為，備兵以抗法。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guofan first arrived, the people of Tianjin thought he would reverse Chonghou's actions and prepared troops to resist France.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan first arrived, Tianjin residents expected him to reverse Chonghou's course and prepared troops to resist the French.

sentences.zh: 然當是時，海內初定，湘軍已散遣，天津咫尺京畿，民、教相閧，此小事不足啟兵端，而津民爭怨之。

translations.literal: Yet at that time the realm had just been pacified, the Hunan army had been disbanded, Tianjin was close to the capital, and commoners and Christians clashed—this small matter was not worth opening hostilities, yet the people of Tianjin all blamed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the empire had only just been pacified, the Hunan army disbanded, and Tianjin lay close to the capital; a clash between residents and Christians was not worth war, yet Tianjin blamed him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 平生故舊持高論者，日移書譙讓，省館至毀所署楹帖，而國籓深維中外兵勢強弱，和戰利害，惟自引咎，不一辯也。

translations.literal: Old friends who held lofty views sent letters daily reproaching him; provincial lodges even tore down the couplets he had inscribed. Yet Zeng Guofan weighed deeply the relative strength of Chinese and foreign forces and the gains and losses of peace and war, and only blamed himself, offering no defense.
translations.idiomatic: Old friends who held lofty views wrote daily to reproach him; provincial lodges even tore down his inscribed couplets. Yet Zeng Guofan weighed the balance of Chinese and foreign military power and the costs of peace and war, blamed only himself, and offered no defense.

sentences.zh: 丁日昌因上奏曰：「自古局外議論，不諒局中艱苦，一唱百和，亦足以熒上聽，撓大計。

translations.literal: Ding Richang therefore memorialized: "From antiquity, opinions from outside the situation fail to understand the hardships within; one voice is taken up by a hundred, and this is enough to dazzle the sovereign's hearing and upset great plans.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Richang memorialized: "From antiquity, outsiders fail to grasp the hardships of those inside the affair; one voice is echoed by a hundred, enough to mislead the throne and upset great plans.

sentences.zh: 卒之事勢決裂，國家受無窮之累，而局外不與其禍，反得力持清議之名，臣實痛之！

translations.literal: In the end the situation ruptures, the state suffers endless burdens, while those outside share none of the calamity and instead gain the name of upholding pure opinion—your servant is truly pained!
translations.idiomatic: In the end affairs rupture, the state bears endless loss, while outsiders share none of the calamity yet win renown for upholding pure opinion—your servant is deeply pained!

sentences.zh: 國籓既負重謗，疾益劇，乃召鴻章治其獄，踰月事定，如初議。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan, now bearing heavy slander and his illness growing worse, summoned Hongzhang to handle the case; within a month the affair was settled as in the original proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing heavy slander and growing gravely ill, Zeng Guofan summoned Li Hongzhang to handle the case; within a month the affair was settled along the original lines.

sentences.zh: 會兩江缺出，遂調補江南，而以鴻章督直隸。

translations.literal: When a vacancy opened in the Two Jiangs, he was transferred to fill Jiangnan, and Hongzhang was made governor-general of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: When a vacancy opened in the Two Jiangs, he was transferred to Jiangnan, and Li Hongzhang was made governor-general of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 江南人聞其至，焚香以迎。

translations.literal: When the people of Jiangnan heard he was coming, they burned incense to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Jiangnan learned he was coming, they burned incense to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 以亂後經籍就熸，設官書局印行，校刊皆精審。

translations.literal: Because after the rebellion the classics and histories had nearly perished, he established an official publishing bureau to print them; collation and editing were all meticulous.
translations.idiomatic: With classics and histories nearly lost after the rebellion, he established an official publishing bureau; its editions were meticulously collated.

sentences.zh: 禮聘名儒為書院山長，其幕府亦極一時之選，江南文化遂比隆盛時。

translations.literal: He ceremonially invited renowned scholars as heads of academies; his staff also gathered the finest men of the age, and Jiangnan culture thus rivaled its most flourishing period.
translations.idiomatic: He ceremonially invited renowned scholars to head academies; his staff gathered the finest men of the age, and Jiangnan culture rivaled its most flourishing era.

sentences.zh: 國籓為人威重，美鬚髯，目三角有棱。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan as a man was imposing and grave, with a fine beard and moustache and triangular eyes with sharp angles.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan was imposing in bearing, with a fine beard and moustache and sharp, angular eyes.

sentences.zh: 每對客，注視移時不語，見者竦然，退則記其優劣，無或爽者。

translations.literal: Whenever he received guests he would gaze at them for a long time without speaking; those who saw this were awed. After they left he would record their strengths and weaknesses, never missing the mark.
translations.idiomatic: When receiving guests he would gaze at them for a long time without speaking, awing all who met him; after they left he recorded their strengths and weaknesses, never erring in his judgment.

sentences.zh: 天性好文，治之終身不厭，有家法而不囿於一師。

translations.literal: By nature he loved learning and pursued it all his life without weariness; he had a family tradition yet was not confined to one teacher.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved learning and pursued it all his life without weariness; he had a family tradition of scholarship yet was not bound to one school.

sentences.zh: 其論學兼綜漢、宋，以謂先王治世之道，經緯萬端，一貫之以禮。

translations.literal: In scholarship he combined Han Learning and Song Learning, holding that the way of the ancient kings in governing the age, though woven of ten thousand strands, was unified by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: His scholarship combined Han and Song learning; he held that the ancient kings' way of governing, though woven of countless strands, was unified by ritual.

sentences.zh: 惜秦蕙田五禮通考闕食貨，乃輯補鹽課、海運、錢法、河堤為六卷；

translations.literal: Regretting that Qin Huitian's Comprehensive Study of the Five Rites lacked the section on food and wealth, he compiled supplements on the salt tax, sea transport, currency, and river dikes in six volumes;
translations.idiomatic: Regretting that Qin Huitian's Comprehensive Study of the Five Rites lacked a section on food and wealth, he compiled supplements on the salt tax, sea transport, currency, and river dikes in six volumes;

sentences.zh: 又慨古禮殘闕無軍禮，軍禮要自有專篇，如戚敬元所紀者。

translations.literal: he also lamented that ancient ritual was damaged and incomplete, lacking military ritual, which ought to have its own special section, as Qi Jingyuan recorded.
translations.idiomatic: he also lamented that ancient ritual was incomplete without military rites, which ought to have their own section, as Qi Jingyuan had recorded.

sentences.zh: 論者謂國籓所訂營制、營規，其於軍禮庶幾近之。

translations.literal: Commentators say that the camp regulations and rules Zeng Guofan drew up came close to military ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that the camp regulations Zeng Guofan drew up came close to true military ritual.

sentences.zh: 晚年頗以清靜化民，俸入悉以養士。

translations.literal: In his later years he largely transformed the people through quiet purity and devoted his entire salary to supporting scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he sought to transform the people through quiet moral example and devoted his entire salary to supporting scholars.

sentences.zh: 老儒宿學，群歸依之。

translations.literal: Old Confucians and established scholars all gathered under him.
translations.idiomatic: Veteran scholars and established Confucians all gathered under his patronage.

sentences.zh: 尤知人，善任使，所成就薦拔者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at knowing men and employing them well; those he advanced and recommended cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at judging men and employing them well; those he advanced and recommended are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 一見輒品目其材，悉當。

translations.literal: At a single meeting he would assess their talent, and in every case he was right.
translations.idiomatic: At a single meeting he would assess a man's talent, and he was never wrong.

sentences.zh: 時舉先世耕讀之訓，教誡其家。

translations.literal: He often cited the ancestral teaching of farming and reading to instruct his family.
translations.idiomatic: He often cited his ancestors' teaching of farming and reading to instruct his household.

sentences.zh: 遇將卒僚吏若子弟然，故雖嚴憚之，而樂為之用。

translations.literal: He treated generals, soldiers, and staff officials like his own sons and younger brothers; therefore though they stood in awe of him, they were glad to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: He treated officers and staff like his own sons and brothers; though they stood in awe of him, they were glad to serve him.

sentences.zh: 居江南久，功德最盛。

translations.literal: He dwelt long in Jiangnan, and his merit and virtue there were greatest.
translations.idiomatic: He dwelt long in Jiangnan, where his merit and beneficence were greatest.

sentences.zh: 論曰：國籓事功本於學問，善以禮運。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Zeng Guofan's achievements and merit rested on learning, and he was skilled in moving affairs through ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Zeng Guofan's achievements rested on learning, and he was skilled in moving affairs through ritual.

sentences.zh: 公誠之心，尤足格眾。

translations.literal: His heart of public sincerity was especially able to transform the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: His heart of public sincerity was especially able to win men over.

sentences.zh: 其治軍行政，務求蹈實。

translations.literal: In governing armies and administration he strove for what was solid and practical.
translations.idiomatic: In military and civil administration he strove for what was solid and practical.

sentences.zh: 凡規畫天下事，久無不驗，世皆稱之，至謂漢之諸葛亮、唐之裴度、明之王守仁，殆無以過，何其盛歟！

translations.literal: Whatever he planned for affairs under heaven, in time none failed to be verified; the age all praised him, even saying that of Han's Zhuge Liang, Tang's Pei Du, and Ming's Wang Shouren he was scarcely surpassed—how grand!
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he planned for the empire was eventually vindicated; the age praised him, comparing him to Zhuge Liang of Han, Pei Du of Tang, and Wang Yangming of Ming—how grand his reputation!

sentences.zh: 國籓又嘗取古今聖哲三十三人，畫像贊記，以為師資，其平生志學大端，具見於此。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan also once took thirty-three sages and worthies of past and present, made portraits with encomia and records, and took them as teachers; the great outlines of his lifelong aspirations and learning are fully seen in this.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan also chose thirty-three sages and worthies of past and present, made portraits with encomia, and took them as his teachers—the great outlines of his lifelong aspirations are fully seen in this.

sentences.zh: 至功成名立，汲汲以薦舉人才為己任，疆臣閫帥，幾遍海內。

translations.literal: When merit was complete and fame established, he eagerly made recommending talent his own task; frontier ministers and commanders-in-chief were nearly all spread across the realm through him.
translations.idiomatic: Once his fame was secure, he eagerly made recommending talent his chief task; frontier governors and commanders throughout the realm were largely his protégés.

sentences.zh: 以人事君，皆能不負所知。

translations.literal: In serving the sovereign through men, all were able not to betray what he had known in them.
translations.idiomatic: In serving the throne through the men he chose, none betrayed the trust he had placed in them.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 中興以來，一人而已。

translations.literal: Since the restoration, there has been only this one man.
translations.idiomatic: Since the restoration, there has been only this one man.
